I, Ramesh Kumar, son of Shyam Lal, resident of Sector 12, Rohini, Delhi, hereby state that on 15th January 2024 at around 9:30 PM, I witnessed my neighbour Vikram Singh brutally attacking my brother Sunil Kumar with a sharp knife near the community park. Vikram stabbed Sunil multiple times in the chest and abdomen. Sunil fell to the ground bleeding profusely. I immediately rushed to help him and called an ambulance. Sunil was taken to Baba Saheb Ambedkar Hospital where doctors declared him dead at 10:15 PM. Vikram fled from the spot immediately after the attack. There was a property dispute between them regarding the boundary wall. I request strict action against Vikram Singh.

I, Ramesh Kumar, resident of House No. 45, Kavi Nagar, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, hereby state that on 12th January 2025 at around 10:30 PM, my brother Suresh Kumar aged 32 years was returning home from his shop in Sahibabad. Near the railway crossing on GT Road, three unidentified persons stopped him and demanded money. When my brother refused and tried to resist, one of the accused persons pulled out a knife and stabbed him multiple times in his chest and abdomen. The accused persons also snatched his gold chain worth Rs. 85,000 and mobile phone Samsung Galaxy S21 valued at Rs. 45,000 from him. They fled on a black motorcycle bearing registration number UP-14-AB-5678. My brother was rushed to Yashoda Hospital where doctors declared him brought dead at 11:15 PM. I suspect the involvement of one Pappu alias Raju who had a property dispute with my brother. This incident has caused severe mental trauma to our entire family.

I, Inspector Rajesh Kumar, Anti-Corruption Bureau, Pune, hereby record that based on a trap operation conducted on 15th March 2024, we apprehended Mr. Sunil Patil, Assistant Municipal Commissioner, Pune Municipal Corporation, while accepting a bribe of Rs. 5,00,000 from Mr. Anil Deshmukh, Director of M/s Skyline Constructions Private Limited, having its registered office at Shivaji Nagar, Pune. The phenolphthalein powder test conducted on Mr. Patil's hands turned pink, confirming the acceptance of tainted currency notes. Both Mr. Sunil Patil and Mr. Anil Deshmukh were arrested. The company records and relevant documents were seized from the office of M/s Skyline Constructions Private Limited.

I belong to the Scheduled Caste community (Meghwal) and the accused intentionally insulted and intimidated me on the grounds of my caste. I request appropriate legal action against the accused.

I, Constable Rajesh Kumar, stationed at Sadar Police Station, Meerut, report that on 15th March 2024 at approximately 3:30 PM, near Suraj Kund Market, an unlawful assembly of around 25-30 persons gathered with the common object of obstructing traffic and causing public disturbance. The assembly, led by accused Vikram Singh, Ramesh Yadav, and Mohit Sharma, became violent when traffic police attempted to clear the road. The mob pelted stones at police personnel, damaging PCR vehicle UP-14-C-5678, and assaulted Head Constable Sunil Verma with lathis, causing him grievous injuries to his head and arms. They also forcibly stopped and damaged a private bus (UP-14-T-9823), breaking its windshield and side mirrors. The rioters raised slogans and used force to prevent vehicular movement for over two hours. Medical examination of HC Sunil Verma was conducted at District Hospital. The accused persons fled when additional police force arrived. Property damage estimated at Rs. 45,000.

I, Sub-Inspector Rajesh Kumar, Police Station Kotwali, District Meerut, U.P., received credible information on 14th March 2024 at 1630 hours that one Vikram Singh Rathore, aged 42 years, resident of Shastri Nagar, Meerut, along with his associates Manoj Tiwari and Ashok Sharma, organized an unauthorized public meeting near Jama Masjid Chowk on 13th March 2024 around 1900 hours. During this gathering, the accused Vikram Singh delivered an inflammatory speech using a loudspeaker, deliberately making derogatory remarks against the Muslim community, alleging that they were conspiring to change the demographic character of the locality. He stated, 'These people are outsiders who want to grab our land and impose their ways on us. We must unite and drive them out before it is too late.' The accused further distributed pamphlets containing false and malicious content aimed at creating hatred between Hindu and Muslim communities. Witness Mohd. Salim, shopkeeper at the Chowk, stated that approximately 150-200 persons gathered and many became agitated. The accused Manoj Tiwari instigated the crowd by shouting slogans like 'Bahar nikalo inko' and waved a stick menacingly toward Muslim-owned shops. Accused Ashok Sharma was seen video-recording the speech and uploading it on social media platforms including Facebook and WhatsApp groups. On 14th March morning, tension escalated when some unidentified persons pelted stones at two shops owned by Rashid Ahmed and Imran Khan, causing damage worth approximately Rs. 45,000. The situation required deployment of additional police force. All three accused are absconding. Investigation is underway.

I suspect Salman Sheikh either knowingly passed counterfeit currency or is part of a larger racket. On 13th March 2024, I went to State Bank of India, M.I. Road branch to deposit cash. The bank cashier detected three more fake Rs. 500/- notes totaling Rs. 1500/- in my collection. I do not know how these entered my cash box but suspect the same accused persons circulated more fake notes in the market. On 14th March 2024 evening, my neighbour shopkeeper Sunil Agarwal informed me that Vikram Singh and Deepak Sharma had threatened him to keep quiet about fake currency or face consequences when he questioned them. They also cheated another shopkeeper Mohan Lal by giving him a fake Rs. 200/- stamp paper in exchange for goods worth Rs. 180/- on 13th March 2024. I request strict action against the accused for circulating counterfeit currency and stamps.

The tainted currency notes totaling Rs. 3,50,000/- were recovered from his drawer. The accused also possessed unaccounted cash of Rs. 1,20,000/- in his personal locker at the office. During interrogation, the accused attempted to offer Rs. 50,000/- to the investigating officer to suppress the matter. Witnesses: 1) Suresh Naik, 2) Mohan Rane.

I, Rajesh Kumar Verma, Sub-Inspector posted at Kotwali Police Station, Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, hereby lodge this complaint. On 15th March 2023, I was assigned to investigate allegations against Constable Vikas Tiwari (Badge No. 4872) regarding misappropriation of seized property. During investigation, I discovered that on 8th February 2023, Constable Tiwari had seized a gold chain weighing approximately 50 grams valued at Rs. 2,45,000 and cash amount of Rs. 85,000 from one Mohan Lal during a raid at his residence in Lashkar area under Case Crime No. 45/2023. The seized property was to be deposited in the Malkhana as per procedure. However, upon verification of Malkhana records on 14th March 2023, it was found that only Rs. 40,000 cash was deposited and no gold chain was entered. When confronted, Constable Tiwari initially claimed the chain was fake and disposed of, but the seizure memo clearly described it as genuine gold. Further inquiry revealed he had sold the gold chain through a jeweller and retained Rs. 45,000 cash for personal use. This constitutes dishonest misappropriation of property entrusted to him as a public servant. The accused has betrayed the trust reposed in him and caused wrongful loss to the complainant Mohan Lal and wrongful gain to himself.

I, Inspector Rajesh Kumar, S.H.O. Police Station Sadar, District Jhansi, U.P., received credible information on 15th March 2024 that one Vijay Singh Tomar, aged 42 years, resident of House No. 234, Civil Lines, Jhansi, is in possession of excessive firearms. During the search, we recovered five firearms from a locked steel almirah in the bedroom: (1) .32 bore revolver (licensed), (2) 12 bore double barrel gun (licensed), (3) .315 bore rifle (Serial No. R-8821), (4) 9mm pistol (Serial No. P-4432), and (5) another .32 bore revolver (Serial No. RV-7765). The accused could not produce any licence or authorization for the three additional firearms. The accused admitted that he acquired these extra firearms over the past two years from various sources but failed to obtain proper licences. All five firearms along with 150 rounds of assorted ammunition were seized under panchnama. The case presents a clear violation of the statutory limit of two firearms per licence holder.

I, Inspector Rajesh Kumar, PS Sadar Bazar, Meerut, report that on 18/03/2023 at approximately 14:30 hours, acting on confidential information, a raid was conducted at Shop No. 47, Shastri Market, Meerut. The shop owner, one Mohd. Salim s/o Abdul Rehman, age 42 years, r/o Qazi Mohalla, Meerut, was found operating an unauthorized workshop for repair and modification of firearms. During search, we recovered 3 country-made pistols in various stages of repair, 2 licensed .32 bore revolvers being illegally modified to increase barrel length, drilling and cutting tools, 17 live cartridges of .315 bore, and hand-written ledgers showing sale transactions of repaired weapons. The accused could not produce any valid Arms Dealer License or Gunsmith License under the Arms Act, 1959. He admitted to repairing firearms for customers without licence for the past eight months and charging Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 5,000 per weapon. One customer, Vikram Singh, was present at the time of raid to collect a repaired pistol. Vikram Singh possessed a valid licence for a different weapon but not for the pistol being collected, creating ambiguity whether he was complicit in the unlicensed repair activity or merely a customer. I, Head Constable Rajesh Kumar, posted at Sadar Police Station, Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, received information from informer Suresh Yadav on 15th January 2024 at 14:30 hours that one Mohit Sharma, resident of Shastri Nagar, Meerut, has sold a country-made pistol to Deepak Verma, who does not possess any valid arms licence. On verification, it was found that Mohit Sharma holds a valid licence for the said pistol bearing number 12345/UP/2020, but Deepak Verma has no licence to possess any firearm. Mohit Sharma knowingly transferred the weapon to an unauthorised person for Rs. 25,000 on 10th January 2024 near Begum Bridge. Both accused persons have been apprehended.

I, Constable Rajesh Kumar, posted at Sadar Police Station, Meerut, hereby report that on 14th January 2025 at approximately 16:30 hours, during routine patrolling near Begum Bridge, we intercepted one Mohd. Salim s/o Rafiq Ahmad, resident of Mohalla Lisari Gate, Meerut. Upon search, he was found in possession of one country-made pistol (.315 bore) and three live cartridges. During interrogation, the accused disclosed that he had purchased the said firearm from one Vikram Singh s/o Balwant Singh, resident of Kharkhauda, Meerut, for a sum of Rs. 15,000/- on 10th January 2025. Further investigation revealed that Vikram Singh does not possess any valid arms licence and had knowingly sold the firearm to Mohd. Salim, who is also not entitled to possess any firearm as per Arms Act provisions. Vikram Singh was subsequently apprehended from his residence. Both the accused persons admitted to the illegal transfer and possession. The firearm and cartridges have been seized and sent for ballistic examination.

I, Constable Rajesh Kumar, posted at Kotwali Police Station, Meerut, report that on 12th January 2025 at approximately 14:30 hours, acting on credible intelligence, a raid was conducted at the residence of one Salman Qureshi, aged 38 years, residing at House No. 47, Shastri Nagar, Meerut. During the search, one country-made pistol (.315 bore) and four live cartridges were recovered from his possession. Upon interrogation, the accused admitted that he had purchased the said firearm from one Vikram Singh, aged 42 years, resident of Village Rataul, Meerut, approximately three months ago for Rs. 18,000. Further investigation revealed that Vikram Singh possessed a valid arms licence for one double-barrel gun only, and was not authorised to possess or transfer the recovered pistol. Vikram Singh knowingly sold the unlicensed firearm to Salman Qureshi, who does not hold any arms licence and is not entitled to possess any firearm. Both accused were arrested. The weapon and ammunition have been seized and sent for ballistic examination. The act of Vikram Singh amounts to illegal transfer of arms to an unauthorised person, while Salman Qureshi is liable for unlicensed possession.

I, Inspector Rajesh Kumar, Police Station Kotwali, District Meerut, record the following statement of complainant Shri Anil Verma s/o Late Ram Prakash Verma, r/o House No. 45, Shastri Nagar, Meerut. The complainant states that on 12th March 2024, he received credible information that one Salman Khan s/o Rashid Khan, r/o Mohalla Qazi Pada, Meerut, who holds a valid arms licence for one .32 bore revolver, has been illegally transferring firearms to unauthorised persons for monetary consideration. On 15th March 2024 at approximately 3:30 PM, our informer informed that Salman Khan would be transferring a country-made pistol to one Deepak alias Deepu s/o Raju Singh, r/o Lohiya Nagar, who does not possess any arms licence. A raid was conducted near Begum Bridge at 4:15 PM. Salman Khan was apprehended while handing over one country-made .315 bore pistol along with three live cartridges to Deepak in exchange for Rs. 35,000 cash. Both accused were arrested on the spot. During search, Salman Khan was also found carrying his licensed .32 bore revolver loaded with six live cartridges but was using it to threaten our constable Manoj Sharma during arrest, saying 'Main tumhe thok dunga'. Deepak confessed he intended to use the pistol to settle a property dispute with his cousin Vikram Singh. Recovery memo was prepared. Seized items include one country-made pistol, three live cartridges of .315 bore, one .32 bore revolver, six live cartridges of .32 bore, and cash Rs. 35,000. The accused Salman Khan has violated Arms Act by transferring arms to an unauthorised person. Deepak has acquired firearm without licence. Investigation is ongoing.

On 18th March 2024 at approximately 3:30 PM, I along with constables Akhilesh Yadav and Ramesh Chaudhary conducted a raid at the accused's premises. We found the accused in the act of handing over one country-made pistol (.315 bore) and four live cartridges to one Javed Ansari, resident of Begampur. Upon inquiry, Javed Ansari could not produce any valid arms licence. The accused Salman Khan admitted that he had sold three other firearms in the past two months to various persons without verifying their licence status. He further admitted to possessing a total of five unlicensed firearms at his residence, of which we recovered three more pistols and twenty-two live cartridges. The accused knowingly transferred the weapon to Javed Ansari despite being aware that the recipient had no legal entitlement to possess firearms. Both accused persons have been detained. The seized firearms and ammunition are being sent for forensic examination.

Acting on credible intelligence, a raid was conducted at the residence of accused Irfan Ahmed, aged 38 years, residing at House No. 47, Shastri Nagar, Meerut. During the search, we recovered one country-made pistol (.315 bore) and six live cartridges from his possession. The accused does not possess any valid arms licence. Upon interrogation, the accused confessed that he had procured the pistol from one Salim Khan of Bulandshahr on 5th March 2024 for Rs. 15,000. Further investigation revealed that the accused had transferred the same pistol to one Deepak Verma, aged 25 years, of Modinagar on 8th March 2024 for Rs. 18,000, knowing fully well that Deepak Verma did not possess any arms licence and was not entitled to possess firearms. The accused also admitted to selling two other country-made pistols to unknown persons in the past month. Deepak Verma was subsequently apprehended from his residence and the pistol was recovered from him. He confessed to planning to use the weapon to threaten his business rival, Ramesh Yadav. During the raid at Irfan Ahmed's house, we also recovered Rs. 45,000 in cash suspected to be proceeds from illegal arms trade. Both accused have been arrested and the arms and ammunition have been seized.

Arjun Yadav, as per the accused's statement, does not possess any valid arms licence himself but has been engaged in selling such weapons to persons who are not entitled to possess them. The accused Vikram Singh further disclosed that Arjun Yadav had informed him that he had sold similar firearms to at least three other persons in the past two months, none of whom held valid licences. Based on this information, we proceeded to the residence of Arjun Yadav at Lalkurti and apprehended him. Upon search of his premises, we recovered two more country-made pistols (.315 bore) and 12 live cartridges. Arjun Yadav could not produce any licence for possession or sale of arms. He admitted to transferring firearms to unauthorised persons for monetary gain. Both the accused persons and the recovered arms and ammunition are being produced before the court.

I, Rajesh Kumar, Food Safety Officer, FSSAI, District Pune, submit this complaint against M/s NutriGlow Health Products Pvt. Ltd., having its office at Plot No. 45, MIDC Industrial Area, Bhosari, Pune. On 15th March 2024, during market surveillance, I noticed television advertisements and print media campaigns for their product 'NutriGlow Immunity Plus Powder'. The advertisements claimed that the product 'cures diabetes within 30 days' and 'eliminates all heart diseases permanently'. Upon inspection of their premises on 18th March 2024, I seized samples and reviewed their advertising materials. The product label and FSSAI licence show it is registered only as a 'health supplement' under category 1.3.2.1, not as a medicine. Laboratory analysis report dated 22nd March 2024 confirms the product contains only vitamins and minerals in permissible limits, with no therapeutic ingredients. The company has been deliberately publishing false claims to mislead consumers into believing the food product has medicinal properties, which it does not possess. Additionally, I found they were operating a separate manufacturing unit at the same premises without obtaining a separate FSSAI licence for that facility. The misleading claims violate Section 53 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the unlicensed unit violates Section 31(1) of the same Act.

We seized 500 units of the product valued at Rs. 2,50,000 and advertising materials. The company has been misleading consumers through false advertisements across print media and social media platforms since October 2023, causing potential health risks and financial loss to approximately 2,000 customers who purchased based on these fraudulent claims.

The misleading advertisements were also displayed on large posters inside the shop premises. The product batch number is BP2024031, manufacturing date 01/02/2024. Samples have been collected and sealed for laboratory analysis. Such false claims mislead consumers and violate food safety regulations. The accused deliberately published misleading advertisements to attract customers and increase sales.
